You want to move Private Island Party from BigCommerce to WooCommerce and launch soon, before your BigCommerce store expires. We rebuild your current look on WooCommerce with the improvements in §2 and §3. Both options have the same scope; they differ only in speed. Option 1 is a rush job, ready in 6 days, with a rush fee. Option 2 runs on our standard schedule, takes 10 days or more and has no rush fee. This document lists what we'd change, what it costs, and what we need from you on day one (§7).

1

Why LitOS

One teamLitOS and LitExtension are part of the same company, LitGroup. The people moving your data and the people building your store work together, so your data is mapped to how your theme displays it, in the admin and on the storefront.

2.1 Header and menu

TodayThe delivery banner, wholesale terms, logo and badges are one picture. We'd cut out the logo and rebuild the rest as text, so it's sharp on phones, readable by Google and easy for you to edit.

TodayThe bar under the header holds only the phone number and social icons. We'd add the main navigation menu here.

2.2 Homepage categories

TodaySubcategories such as Customized Hats and Customized Sunglasses sit in a side list. We'd show a few of them as tabs in the empty space next to the block title, and add a separate section listing your main categories.

2.3 Footer and pages

TodayThe footer lists every article. These are set up as pages; we'd move them to the blog and stop listing them in the footer.

TodayPages like these (returns, terms, wholesale application, privacy) stay as pages and in the footer. The fundraiser item crossed out in red would go to the blog. Final list to confirm (§7).

3

Features

3.1 Product options and personalization

TodayOne product uses style choices, fonts, color swatches, a custom text box and a logo upload, most of them required. All of this has to work the same way on WooCommerce.

We rebuild these fields with Advanced Product Fields Pro: required fields, color swatches, text input and logo upload. Swatches and file upload are in the Pro version only (§9). The customer's choices show on the order, so you can produce it.

3.2 Discounts

We set up Discount Rules for WooCommerce. Its free version covers quantity-based bulk discounts; the Pro version is only needed for rules like category or customer-group discounts (§7).

3.3 Product cards

Cards get "Add to cart" and "Quick view" on hover, with the layout redesigned to fit. Quick view comes with Blocksy Pro (§8, §9). We also fix smaller UI issues across the store as we build.

3.4 Live chat and email

Live chat: you send us your Tawk.to code and we add it to the site. Email: we set up an SMTP plugin so order and account emails reach the inbox instead of spam.

5

Your data, customers and Google rankings

Your concernHow it's handled
Google rankingsLitExtension's 301 redirect option sends every old product and category URL to its new page. It's a paid option when you buy the migration; we recommend it, otherwise these redirects are made by hand. For pages, blog posts (including the pages moved to the blog in §2.3), SEO titles and the new sitemap, we give you a step-by-step guide. Some movement in rankings in the first weeks is normal.
Orders during the moveYour BigCommerce site stays live until you switch the domain. Just before launch, LitExtension moves the orders, customers and products added in the meantime (included as long as the new data is no more than 5% of the original migration). LitExtension reads from your BigCommerce store, so it must stay active until this last move is done (§7).
Wrong or missing dataWe check the migrated data in the admin and on the storefront, and work with LitExtension to correct anything that's wrong or missing.
Customer loginsWe confirm with LitExtension whether customer passwords can move from BigCommerce. If they can't, customers set a new password on their first sign-in.

Open questions

#QuestionWhy it matters
1Option 1 (6 days) or Option 2 (10+ days)?Sets the price and the launch date.
2On what date does your BigCommerce store expire?The migration and the final data move must finish before then. It sets the kick-off and launch dates.
3Where will the WooCommerce site be hosted? Do you already have WordPress hosting?We need hosting to build on. Hosting is paid by you and isn't in the estimate.
4Should the new store enforce your $30 minimum order and 12-piece minimums at checkout?Not in the estimate. It may need an extra plugin and hours, and could affect the timeline.
5Which discount rules do you need (quantity tiers, bulk pricing, coupons)?The free plugin covers quantity tiers; other rules need the Pro version (§9).
6Which categories go in the main menu, and which few show as tabs on the homepage?You have about 15 top-level categories; not all fit in one menu bar.
7Can you confirm which pages stay in the footer (§2.3) and which move to the blog?Sets the footer and the list of redirects you'll add for moved pages (§5).
8Which email account should store emails be sent from?Needed to set up SMTP (§3.4). You enter the account's password yourself.
8

Theme

We build on Blocksy, a fast WordPress theme that works well with WooCommerce, and use Elementor for page layouts such as the homepage. Elementor's free version covers this project. Blocksy needs its Pro version for the product Quick view (§3.3). Licenses are bought in your name (§9).
